## About me

Adrian Waddell. Senior Principal Software Engineer for Pharma & Life
Sciences at Posit, PBC.

Before Posit:

- PhD in Statistics, University of Waterloo, Canada.
- At **Roche**, led a project building R-based analysis and reporting tools
  for clinical trial analysis, some of them now part of pharmaverse.
- At **Genentech gRED**, led R and Python environment management for the
  research HPC. EasyBuild, Gentoo Prefix, Lmod, Slurm, and a bespoke R
  package manager.

## Where this material comes from

The gRED environment:

- Bespoke R package manager, following the CRAN and Bioconductor release
  model
- Shared R environment deployments
- 5,500 R packages, from CRAN, Bioconductor, and internal sources, resolved
  and built as one set
- Two releases a year, aligned with the Bioconductor schedule
- Daily snapshots, so an analysis could be pinned to a date


## What you will learn

- Where R lives on disk, how it starts up, and how it finds packages
- What to check first when a user reports that a package will not install
- How to build a package set you can test, ship, and update deliberately

We work mostly in a terminal. The aim is to know which layer a problem
lives in, not to memorise flags.

## Discussion

Block 7 is a scheduled slot for real-world production issues, discussed as
a group.

Bring something concrete: a configuration you inherited and do not trust,
an upgrade that went badly, a rule you cannot justify to an auditor.

If your question fits the block we are in, ask it there rather than waiting.
The timings have slack for it.

## The lab environment

We use the `rocker/r-base` container:

```bash
docker pull rocker/r-base
docker run --rm -it --name rlab rocker/r-base bash
```

`--rm` deletes the container on exit. Several blocks start from a fresh
container.

::: {.note}
[Before we start]{.note-label}
Please run the `docker pull` now. The image is about 400&nbsp;MB
([Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/rocker/r-base/tags)).
:::

## No Docker? Use Posit Cloud

If you cannot run Docker or Podman, you should have an invitation to a Posit
Cloud workspace:

[login.posit.cloud](https://login.posit.cloud/)

It gives you R, a terminal, and a writable user library.

::: {.note}
[No root]{.note-label}
You cannot `apt-get install` system dependencies or write to
`$(R RHOME)/etc` and `/opt`. Demos that do (site configuration in block 2,
system requirements in block 4, the local repository in block 6) are
watch-along.
:::

## Two windows, one container

You can keep a second shell open on the same container, for example to look at the
filesystem while R is running.

```bash
docker exec -it rlab bash
```

Inside, `R` starts an interactive session and `q()` or `Ctrl-D` leaves it.

## Reference documentation

| Manual | What it answers |
|---|---|
| [R Installation and Administration](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html) | Build flags, libraries, environment variables, site configuration |
| `?EnvVar` and the R-admin [environment variable index](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Environment-variable-index) | The environment variables R reads |
| [Writing R Extensions](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html) | `DESCRIPTION` fields, dependency types, what `R CMD check` checks |
| [CRAN Repository Policy](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html) | What CRAN will and will not accept, and why archiving happens |
| `?Startup`, `?.libPaths`, `?install.packages` | The same material, offline, versioned with your R |
